searchText: Meh, NASDAQ is about as useful as USD IMO. What comparison would you like to see? Dumping everything into sqlite is pretty easy. Some proxy for "cost of energy". Price of oil? On log scale this time Using `Crude Oil Mar 22 (CL=F)`, whatever that is. I don't commodity at all 😅 Is that both priced in USD? Yes. Will do! If you're looking for more stuff about crypto finance specifically, this probably isn't the right server. This conversation is _wildly_ off topic lol If you're looking to connect with people about Ethereum development and research, this is definitely the right place! Say hi in the <#595701895700676644> channel and talk a little about yourself and what you're hoping to find. `Price of ETH` divided by `Price of Oil`, back on a linear scale. That is the price of oil for march 2022 delivery, so the data point for 2018 isn't a true representation of the price of oil at that time as it would be factoring in the cost of storing that oil all the way up to march 2022 I would recommend using CL1 ticker which is a forward roll of the prompt oil contract: https://www.bloomberg.com/quote/CL1:COM So at any given point in time, CL1 will be the price of crude with earliest delivery in the futures market (spot market trades different contracts and delivery is earlier) Hm, I need to get that data in a tractable format. Yahoo finance has a nice CSV export option... is the above price data from yahoo finance? Yahoo calls it March 22 but the historic data would be for the corresponding prompt contract. So you can ignore what I said above if you are pulling the CL data from Yahoo. Yes, that's where I'm grabbing it from Specifically: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL%3DF/history?p=CL%3DF&.tsrc=fin-srch you are looking at the right price then 👍 Looking at the charts, seems like ETH is falling compared to the "price of energy" (or our proxy for it). What does that mean exactly? 😛 With recent geo-political incidents in the Middle East and Russia, hard to tell if the price of oil is going up because of supply / demand or speculation. Maybe use a commodity index instead? It includes commodities like precious metals and agriculture: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EBCOM/
